checks.full_source_review: Read all five full original and historical source records, notes, all 15 starters and the full final proposal. Checked Dutch, English criterion translations, prompts, models, sample omissions/errors, quotes, image briefs/alt text and cue.
checks.batch_check: npm run batch:check -- content/batches/045-proposed.json: Checked 5 items, 0 questions. No failures, no warnings. Five existing IDs are intentional replacements.
checks.count_and_ids: All five supplied IDs retained in the same order. One picture-sequence, one picture-choose, two picture-describe, one video-answer.
checks.metadata: All duo-a2 / a2-spreken, 40 seconds speaking and 10 seconds preparation; domains fit; targetLevelValidated false; no retired type or generated media.
checks.sample_quotes: Ten non-null quotes are verbatim; every sample omits precisely criterion three. Deliberate learner agreement/adjective errors remain comprehensible.
checks.starters: All 15 frames contain ellipses, allow grammatical completion and match the criteria in order; completion tests recorded per item. Original starters unchanged.
checks.visuals: Eight image briefs have exact configured cast traits and Dutch scene alt text. Parcel sequence preserves Karim, parcel and doorway; the ticket pair changes the purchase method in a shared setting. Broken fence and slide supply the playground details.
checks.cue_audio: Sabrina uses configured f-adult. The two-part cue requests appointment time and arrival status; the narrator prompt requests current time separately. Digits absent. Still/audio substitute is disclosed.
checks.sources: No KNM claims, named organisations, addresses or websites. No external fact checks needed for these fictional daily scenes.
checks.level: Models have 29–31 words and maximum sentences of 8–11 words, within the editorial target. No CEFR validation claim.
checks.references: Read AGENTS.md, blueprint, review and author briefs, rubric, content workflow, relevant research passage, illustration/voice configurations and catalogue titles. Used two batch027 comparisons per type because content/exemplars does not exist.

diversity: All five historical broad subjects remain. Parcel handling is a sequence, tram ticket purchase is a preference, the coat and playground scenes ask for descriptions with opinions, and waiting for a technician uses a spoken service question. Two neighbourhood settings are inherited replacements. This batch is not a complete exam form.
author_doubts_decisions: Asking the employee for help is a defensible reason for the preference and does not describe the machine.
The coat ownership mistake is supplied by the prompt; the image need only establish the objects and current scene.
A damaged fence is observable rather than an opinion, so the playground sample truly omits the opinion goal.
The playground model gives one possible opinion; learners need not call it dangerous.
No named businesses require web searches.
media_notes: No media generated or reviewed. After adoption and the hash gate, generate five narrator prompts, one Sabrina cue and eight illustrations. Inspect parcel direction and continuity, the two purchase methods with identical setting/viewpoint, a visible blue coat and phone, and the fence gap beside the slide with the street side clear. Confirm house cast traits in actual output.
limitations: AI editorial review only; A2 remains an unvalidated authoring target.
No calibrated exemplar directory exists; batch027 comparisons are project references.
Actual illustrations and audio still require generation and separate media review.
